questions.question: A patient with right hemiplegia is observed during gait training. The patient performs side stepping towards the hemiplegic side. The physical therapist may expect the patient to compensate for weakened abductors by:

options.B: Lateral trunk flexion towards the hemiplegic side
options.C: Lateral trunk flexion towards the unaffected side
options.D: Hip extension of the hemiplegic side 24

questions.explanation: Weak abductors are compensated by lateral trunk flexion toward the unaffected side.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The permissible 8-hour occupational noise exposure limit is:
questions.explanation: Hearing protection is required above 85 dB.

questions.question: A 25 year old male is diagnosed with a first degree acromioclavicular sprain. The injury occurred two days ago after being checked into the boards while playing hockey. Which of the following would you not expect to be true during the initial examination?

options.A: Increased elevation of the clavicular end of the acromion
options.B: Inability to bring the arm completely across the chest
options.C: Inability to fully abduct the arm throughout the full range of motion
options.D: Point tenderness on palpation of the injury site

questions.explanation: A grade I AC sprain does not produce elevation of the clavicle end; the joint remains stable.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A development examination is completed on an eight month old infant. questions.explanation: At eight months an infant should sit unsupported and have no head lag, so the findings indicate delay.

questions.question: A therapist monitors patient vital signs while exercising in a phase I cardiac rehabilitation program. options.C: Systolic blood pressure decreases by 20 mm Hg from resting level
options.D: Diastolic blood pressure less than 100 mm Hg

questions.question: Exercise causes a significant increase in the body's cardiac output. During mild to moderate exercise what redistribution of the available cardiac output would you expect?

options.C: An increase in coronary and active skeletal muscle blood flow
options.D: A decrease in cerebral and coronary blood flow
